Then in the else branch, `current_tag` would be "1" (since HEAD points to the latest commit which is tagged "1" in my test repo... wait, no).

Let me think again. In my reproduction test repo, the latest commit on master is tagged "1". So after `git clone --depth 1 --no-checkout`, HEAD points to the latest commit which is tagged "1". So `git describe --exact-match --tags HEAD` returns "1".

Now, if `version: '1'` is specified:
- `checkout_param` = "1" (found tag)
- `current_tag` = "1" (HEAD is at the tagged commit)
- With my condition `unless is_eligible_for_caching && !version.nil? && current_tag == version`:
  - `is_eligible_for_caching` is false (no cache_path) â condition is false â checkout HAPPENS â

Good, my fix correctly handles this because `is_eligible_for_caching` is false in the non-caching case, so checkout always happens.

But wait, let me reconsider. There's a subtle issue. What if the requested version is NOT the latest commit? For example, `version: '1'` but the latest commit is tagged "3". Then after `git clone --depth 1 --no-checkout` (which clones only the latest commit), HEAD points to commit tagged "3", so `current_tag` = "3" != "1", and `checkout_param` = "1".
